x: As there was a thick fog during the afternoon we were lucky to get the event run off and all concerned were full of praise for the excellent course arrangements Jim Masters was our first man home and deservedly gained his County Colours by finishing fourth.

… of retaining the trophy by scoring a runaway victory in the fast time of 55mins. 9secs. Chas.Walker 55.02 was 2nd with Jim Masters 3rd in 55.17, the next three placings being P.Bagnall 55.40,D.Brickwood 55.56, and E.…

This was held over a 7 miles course at Aylesford and our lads did well to finish runners up in the team race. Peter Bagnall ran a very good race to finish 7th, then came Jim Masters 18th, Bob Taylor 21st, D.
Next was the Senior Race with a huge field. Our first man home was Jim Masters 21st, followed by Stan Gawler 29th D.

Cornish gained another 3rd place in the 440 yards and Jim Heathfield was second in the 880 yards. Jim Masters ran well in the three miles but did not have sufficient speed at the finish and finished 2nd to J.
Jim Masters finished 8th and so was again invited to represent Surrey in the Inter Counties at Liverpool and we congratulate him on his running in a good class field.
When the field had settled down, Jim Masters was running 3rd with Baker of the local club who eventually beat him and our scoring six were in the first thirty.

Jim Masters unfortunately injured his foot again on the iron hard ground; he had already done so once this season in the Inter Counties. South London proved easy winners with 82 points, Belgrave 2nd. 182 points and T.V.H. 3rd 205 points.
Colin Wilson, S.L.H., led by 7 seconds at the take over, from Jim Masters, but as the S.L.H. second man was not ready, Cliff Roffey went off with a few yards lead.

Jim Masters on the switchback course through Redhill and Earlswood again gave us hope by passing three clubs and taking us up to 6th. Thames Valley, however, were represented by Norris and added 10 more seconds to their lead.
When we eventually caught up with the runners again, (those motor driven coaches are a greater nuisance than the athletic type) we found Jim Masters in command.
A quick switch of Eric Gebbett from the fifth to the fourth leg let in Jim Masters on the Redhill stage which has almost become his own property by divine right.

Jim Masters took the fifth leg and remained in the same position, although losing ground on the teams ahead. Don Maclean who is in great form these days, went off last and with a good effort gained one place to bring us into fifth place.
Jim Masters (23.05). Jim must know every inch of this section of the road and we hoped that his knowledge would help us.
John Moore, Jim Masters and Eric Gebbett were soon prominent and we seemed set for a close win,but we lost points when the leaders took the wrong turning.
Hallowell, Gebbett, Roffey and Shippen were in close attendance and Peter Shipley, our 2nd claim member from Farnham, was about 20yds further back with Jim Masters.
